transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, what finally pushed me to come in is that my eating has just been all over the place lately. Some weeks, I barely even touch dinner. But then other nights, I'll just stand in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets long after everyone else has gone to bed. It's just been very inconsistent, and I figured I should talk to someone about it.
When you barely eat, is that because you are intentionally trying to lose weight or keep from gaining weight?

No, it's not about losing weight at all. I'm not really paying attention to the scale or anything like that. It's just... I don't know, sometimes I just don't have an appetite, or I just don't think about eating. It's not on purpose.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for persistent low or depressed mood to evaluate for a major depressive episode.", "question": "Alongside these changes in your eating, have you been experiencing persistent feelings

Yeah, I have. I go through these stretches where... I don't know, the whole house just feels gray and heavy. I'll just sit at the kitchen table feeling completely empty, even though nothing terrible has actually happened that day. It just sort of hangs over me.
Have you ever had periods where you felt the exact opposite—unusually energetic, wired, or on top of the world, needing much less sleep than usual?

Yeah, I do get like that. There are these periods when I feel... just really bright and completely unstoppable. But then, almost out of nowhere, I can get suddenly furious over something really small. Like, um, if my husband moves my paints, or if he just questions a receipt from the store, I'll just snap and get incredibly angry.
When you go through those stretches of feeling empty and down, how long do they usually last?
Well, um... those gray periods where I just feel empty and guilty, and I lose interest in everything... if I add them all up over the past year, it's been about seven months total.
When one of those gray, empty stretches starts, how long does that single period usually last without a break?

Um, I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't exactly tracked a single one from start to finish. It just feels like once the grayness sets in, it... it drags on for quite a while. But I couldn't give you an exact number of weeks or days or anything like that.
When you have those periods of feeling unusually energetic and unstoppable, how many days in a row does that state typically last?

Um, I really couldn't say for sure. Just like with the down periods, I don't really keep track of the days when I feel like that. It just happens, and I ride it out until it stops, but I've never counted how long it lasts in a row.
During those energetic, unstoppable periods, did they ever cause serious problems with your work or relationships, or lead to hospitalization?

Well, I haven't been hospitalized for it, no. But it does cause issues. Um, I've actually fallen behind on my facilitator training and my private blog work. It's just... my projects and the way I explain things become really hard to organize when I'm like that. And it definitely affects things at home, too. There's been a lot of tension, which has made it a lot harder to just keep up normal routines with my husband.

```json
{"intent": "Determine the overall duration of the alternating mood swings to evaluate for cyclothymia.", "question": "For how many years have you been experiencing this

Um, it's been about two years and five months now. I remember it started around the time the arguments at home really escalated... mostly over my spending and, well, my art projects. So yeah, almost two and a half years.

```json
{"intent": "Determine the longest symptom-free interval to assess cyclothymia criteria.", "question": "Over these past two years, what is the longest

Um, I'm really not sure. I haven't really kept track of the times when nothing is happening. It just feels like I'm always either dealing with the highs or the lows, or just the tension from it all, so... I don't really know if there was ever a long stretch where I felt completely normal. If there was a break, I didn't measure how long it lasted.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for suicidal thoughts or thoughts of death during depressive periods to evaluate for a major depressive episode.", "question": "During those gray, empty periods,

Well, um... on the worst nights, when everything just feels really heavy and empty, I do sometimes think it would be easier if I just didn't wake up. It's just a thought that crosses my mind when things are really bad. But I haven't actually made a plan to hurt myself or anything like that.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for fatigue or loss of energy during depressive periods to evaluate for a major depressive episode.", "question": "During those gray, empty stretches, do you experience overwhelming
No, not really. I mean, I feel empty and down, but I wouldn't say I'm overwhelmingly tired or anything. I just feel kind of blank, but I still have my normal energy levels, for the most part.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for sleep disturbances during depressive periods to evaluate for a major depressive episode.", "question": "During those gray, empty periods, have you had any trouble sleeping
No, my sleep is usually fine. I might toss and turn a bit if I'm feeling really restless, but overall, I don't have a hard time falling asleep or staying asleep during those times.
During those gray, empty periods, do you have trouble concentrating, focusing, or making everyday decisions?

No, I haven't really noticed any issues with that. I mean... I might not have the motivation to do a whole lot when I'm feeling that way, but if I need to read something or make a decision, I can focus just fine. My mind stays pretty clear.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for decreased need for sleep during periods of high energy to evaluate for a manic or hypomanic episode.", "question": "During those times when you feel

When I get like that, yeah, my sleep definitely changes. I can sleep for maybe three or four hours and wake up feeling completely charged. I'll be ready to write blog posts or, you know, plan out new projects before the sun is even up. I just don't feel like I need the rest.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for racing thoughts or flight of ideas during high-energy periods to evaluate criteria for mania or hypomania.", "question": "During those energetic periods, do

Yeah, my thoughts definitely speed up. It's like... they just run so fast that one idea bumps right into the next. I'll be thinking about roses, and then suddenly it's about money, or colors, or messages, or classes. It all just rushes through my head, and I can't really slow them down enough to even explain what I'm thinking to anyone else.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for grandiosity or inflated self-esteem during energetic periods to evaluate for a manic episode.", "question": "During those times when you feel

During those times when I feel really energetic, I definitely feel more confident than usual. Like, I'll become completely sure that my art-therapy workshop is going to change people's lives in a major way. I just know it's going to be huge, even though... well, I haven't actually finished the training for it yet. But in those moments, I feel like I'm meant to do something really important.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for excessive or inappropriate feelings of guilt during down periods to evaluate for a major depressive episode.", "question": "During those gray and empty times

Yeah, I do. When I'm in those gray periods, I just feel so guilty about everything. I can spend hours just sitting there, replaying really small things in my head... like buying an expensive tube of paint pigment, or maybe snapping at my husband over something silly. And I just get this overwhelming feeling that I've completely ruined the whole household because of it. It feels so heavy, like everything is my fault.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for psychomotor agitation or retardation during depressive periods to evaluate for a major depressive episode.", "question": "During those gray, empty periods, have other people noticed

During those gray periods? Um, no, I don't think anyone has said anything about me moving differently. My husband hasn't mentioned me being restless or moving super slow or anything like that. I mostly just sit there feeling awful, but I guess physically I just look normal to other people.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for psychotic symptoms during mood episodes to differentiate bipolar disorder from cyclothymia.", "question": "During your highest or lowest times, did you ever

During my highest or lowest times, did I ever... what exactly? If you mean, like, strange things happening... yeah. When I'm in those really charged, unstoppable stretches—when I'm planning my workshops and barely sleeping—that's when things get kind of weird. I'll read comments online and they feel like... like coded warnings meant just for me. And sometimes, I'll hear my name being called out loud, but there's no one around. It usually happens when I'm feeling that intense energy.
